portfolio.title: Gabriel Pendleton Portfolio
portfolio.summary: Gabriel Pendleton's portfolio is an operating record of product leadership and hands-on building across AI-native products, creator platforms, marketplaces, APIs, integrations, and autonomous systems. It brings together selected product work, AI experiments, professional experience, writing, credentials, and the systems Gabriel is building in public.
portfolio.professionalSummary: Gabriel Pendleton is a Senior Product Leader and two-time founder focused on turning ambiguous opportunities into working products and systems. His work spans zero-to-one strategy, creator platforms, personalization, experimentation, API-first marketplaces, podcast infrastructure, local AI, multi-agent systems, product discovery, and cross-functional delivery.
portfolio.story: Gabriel built the portfolio this way because he has a passion for AI and believes this is an unusually innovative period in technology. He wanted the site to reflect his excitement about where software and AI experiences are going. Instead of making only a traditional digital resume, he wanted the portfolio itself to demonstrate technical ability and product thinking. Its interactive interfaces, AI-powered experiences, visual systems, experimental product concepts, and futuristic interface ideas are part of that demonstration. Gabriel's roots in technology began with video games and interactive experiences, which influenced his decision to make visiting the portfolio feel like an experience rather than a collection of static pages. The result is both a professional portfolio and a showcase of his interests in AI, product development, technical experimentation, and interactive design.

askGabriel.title: Ask Gabriel
askGabriel.summary: Ask Gabriel is the portfolio's RAG-powered knowledge experience. It uses semantic retrieval, embeddings, and vector search to find relevant information in Gabriel's published portfolio knowledge, then generates concise grounded answers with source citations. It is designed to reject weak evidence instead of inventing unsupported personal or professional facts. Conversations remain session-only. Specific providers, models, endpoints, thresholds, deployment configuration, and other private infrastructure are intentionally not public portfolio knowledge.
